title: ASHAs reject government’s assurance; decide to continue protest

ai.summary: Karnataka ASHA workers rejected government assurances on a pay hike and continued their fifth-day protest after talks ended inconclusively.

facts.claim: The second round of talks between the State government and protesting ASHAs ended inconclusively on Saturday, with the workers rejecting the government’s assurance on a pay hike and deciding to continue their agitation, which entered its fifth day.
facts.quote: The second round of talks between the State government and protesting ASHAs ended inconclusively on Saturday, with the workers rejecting the government’s assurance on a pay hike and deciding to continue their agitation, which entered its fifth day.

facts.claim: Health Minister U.T. Khader had invited representatives of the Karnataka State Samyukta ASHA Workers’ Union for discussions.
facts.quote: Health Minister U.T. Khader had invited representatives of the Karnataka State Samyukta ASHA Workers’ Union for discussions.

facts.claim: The talks failed after the Minister said the demand for an increase in remuneration would be discussed during the preparation of the next State Budget.
facts.quote: The talks failed after the Minister said the demand for an increase in remuneration would be discussed during the preparation of the next State Budget.

facts.claim: The workers refused to accept the assurance and decided to continue their protest.
facts.quote: The workers refused to accept the assurance and decided to continue their protest.

facts.claim: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar appealed to the protesting ASHAs to withdraw their agitation, expressing sympathy for their hardships and acknowledging their contribution to the healthcare system.
facts.quote: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar appealed to the protesting ASHAs to withdraw their agitation, expressing sympathy for their hardships and acknowledging their contribution to the healthcare system.

facts.claim: Mr. Shivakumar said the government was considering a comprehensive and lasting solution to their demands and would discuss the matter with the Cabinet before taking an appropriate decision.
facts.quote: Mr. Shivakumar said the government was considering a comprehensive and lasting solution to their demands and would discuss the matter with the Cabinet before taking an appropriate decision.

ai.background_note: ASHA workers in Karnataka have been protesting for a pay hike, with their agitation entering its fifth day after talks with the state government ended inconclusively.
